summary: All three blocking findings are valid implementation/data-path gaps and should be applied in spec repair.

items.title: Prepare hook has no live flow context
items.rationale: The workflow plugin prepare.post hook is required to replace issue-start behavior, but the current prepare lifecycle can run with pre-prepare flow context unless the spec requires re-resolving the newly written flow state.
items.evidence: spec.json R4 and AC5 require prepare.post behavior. Review cites applyLifecycleActionsFromRegistry using ctx.flowState before RunPrepareSpecCommand writes flow.json, so linked issue and hook snapshot may be unavailable.

items.title: Finalize hook has no successful-output or artifact path
items.target: R4 / Design Principles / src/lib/plugin-registry.js runFlowCommandHooks and src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js
items.rationale: The spec requires finalize-cleanup.post candidate extraction and follow-up surfacing, but it does not yet require a durable artifact path or aggregation of successful hook output.
items.evidence: spec.json R4 and data_flow mention finalize-cleanup.post, but no requirement states successful hook return data must be collected or that issue-log/spec artifact paths remain available before worktree teardown.

items.title: Plugin AI fallback lacks a public integration point
items.target: R5 / plugin command and hook context
items.rationale: Workflow publish and ideas behavior depends on AI calls, and the plugin cannot remain external if it must import core internals to resolve or run agents.
items.evidence: spec.json R5 requires plugin.config.workflow.agent overrides but does not require a workflow-neutral public plugin agent API/context. Review identifies buildPluginApi/buildPluginContext as lacking that public integration point.
